newsitem.title: UK: GEC mum on Thomson news, analysts see little impact.
newsitem.headline: GEC mum on Thomson news, analysts see little impact.

text.p: General Electric Plc was unavailable for comment late on Friday to news that the French government has halted the privatisation process of defence electronics group Thomson-CSF.

But analysts say the news may have only a limited impact on GEC's shares since expectations of a Thomson sale were lowered after the June 1 election of the new Socialist government in France. The new government halted the sell off process after taking power.

GEC had put in a bid for Thomson some months ago after being encouraged to do so by "one part" of the French government. But GEC was later rebuffed. Nevertheless, it had remained hopeful of forming some link with the group.

French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's office said in a statement on Friday evening it would propose an alternative solution to build "a French professional and defence-electronics pillar" based on Thomson-CSF instead of privatisation.
George Simpson, GEC managing director, told Reuters on Tuesday that he continued to talk to Thomson but he said "it is difficult to interpret the situation".
"Ideologically it may have been opposed to privatisation, but it is aware of the fact that Thomson's management has been left out to dry on this.
Simpson said the French government "is struggling to live with its ideology and come up with a practical solution" though he still saw GEC as a "natural partner" for Thomson.
Thomson and GEC were seen by many analysts to be the perfect couple for a defence marriage.
Pressure is mounting on European defence players to consolidate to enable them to face stiff competition in world export markets from the U.S. groups which are larger, more powerful and leaner.
On Thursday GEC took a small step towards building European defence alliances by announcing a defence joint venture with Finmeccanica SpA SIFI.L of Italy.
